findings.description: Debug leftovers remain in the library's source, which QUAL-001 marks blocking. The developer's report acknowledges them but leaves them as 'outside the design scope'. QUAL-001 is not scoped to changed files - it applies to the library's source and is a publish gate: the DevTeam 'No debugging leftovers' check already failed on exactly these three lines (run 20261008-135042, proof-report.md lines 36-39). They must be removed (or the violation explicitly accepted by the builder) before this is publishable.
findings.evidence: console.log('SortPlugin: Header clicked. Target:', target); at line 120, console.log('SortPlugin: Interactive element clicked, ignoring sort.'); at line 123 and console.log('SortPlugin: Non-interactive element clicked, proceeding with sort.'); at line 127. This is the only console.* / debugger occurrence in src (grep for console\.(log|debug)|debugger returns exactly these three).
findings.note: The three debug leftovers are gone from the sortable-header click handler in src/Plugins/SortPlugin.ts (git diff: console.log lines at old 120/123/127 removed; current file lines 118-137 contain only the target.closest('input, button, a, [onclick]') guard, its early return and the unchanged sorting logic). A search of src for console\.(log|debug)|debugger returns no matches. The legitimate console.warn (custom sortComparer arity) at src/Plugins/SortPlugin.ts:78 is retained per R3. Verified independently: `npm run build` exits 0 (dist/index.js + dist/index.mjs, banner '"use client";'), `npm run type-check` exits 0, `npm run validate-package` exits 0 with attw reporting node10/node16(CJS)/node16(ESM)/bundler all green and no FalseCJS, and `npx jest src/Plugins/SortPlugin.test.ts` passes 3/3.

findings.description: The new test file follows the existing placement convention, so this is not a regression introduced solely here, but it does add another test artifact to the published dist. LIB-003 says tests in the package leak work in progress; the declarations are empty so the impact is small. Excluding test files from the declaration build (or from the published files) would be the clean fix, but it is pre-existing and LIB-003's automatic check is not set up in this project, so recorded as advisory rather than blocking.
findings.evidence: tsconfig.json includes 'src' and the Rollup @rollup/plugin-typescript config sets declaration: true with declarationDir: 'dist', so the new test is compiled into the published package: the build produces dist/Package.test.d.ts (alongside the pre-existing dist/Build.test.d.ts and every dist/**/*.test.d.ts). package.json 'files' lists 'dist', so these test declaration files ship to consumers.
